standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial objects and the normalised complex
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a simplicial object of an abelian category, the normalised chain complex N, whose n-th term is the quotient of the n-simplices by the degenerate ones.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object computed in the statement (source lines 4014-4018).

standard_prerequisites.name: Eilenberg-MacLane objects
standard_prerequisites.statement: The simplicial object K(A,k) built as the induced object from the skeleton, with K(A,k)_i = 0 for i below k, equal to A in degree k, and nondegenerate simplices only in degree k (the author's definition-eilenberg-maclane and lemma-imshriek-abelian, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the three degree computations of the proof (source lines 4022-4029).

core_obligations: Degrees below k: use K(A,k)_i = 0 for i smaller than k to conclude N(K(A,k))_i = 0 (source lines 4022-4023).
Degree k: use K(A,k)_{k-1} = 0 and K(A,k)_k = A to get N(K(A,k))_k = A (source lines 4024-4025).
Degrees above k: read the vanishing off from the induced-object description of K(A,k) (source lines 4026-4029).

proof_roadmap.step: Settle the degrees below k from the vanishing of the simplicial object there.
Compute the single non-zero term in degree k.
Get the vanishing above k from the induced-object description.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-N-K at source lines 4012-4019: for an object A of an abelian category the normalised chain complex of the Eilenberg-MacLane simplicial object K(A,k) has N(K(A,k))_i equal to A for i = k and zero otherwise. The proof at source lines 4021-4030 is a three-line degree check: for i below k the simplicial object itself vanishes in that degree so the normalised complex does too; in degree k the two ingredients K(A,k)_{k-1} = 0 and K(A,k)_k = A give the single copy of A; and above k the vanishing is read off from the explicit description of K(A,k) as an induced object. It is short and degreewise; the only input is the author's construction of K(A,k).
